request.spec:
A person with a hold in force on the sheet's today (a hold whose dates include today) gets no cut
from any pool, and their share is spread over the other members with a cut in proportion to those
members' shares: each member's cut is the pot times their share divided by the shares of the members
with a cut, added up, rounded half to even, with the remainder to the largest share as before (when
no member is left with a cut, each shows 0.00). The pool's total share and balance are unchanged by
the hold.

agent.result_text:
A person with a hold in force on the sheet's today now gets no cut from any pool, and their share is spread over the other members. `bin/e2e` passes: all 4 tests in the spec.

I only changed the server; the screen needed nothing new:

- **`pool/PoolMember.java`**: each member now has a `held` flag, and a `cut()` check that means "neither retired nor held". I kept the old five-argument constructor, defaulting to not held, so the code that adds members didn't need to change.
- **`pool/PoolRepository.java`**: a new `findAll(sheetId, today)` sets a person member as held when one of their holds covers today. A hold with no from-date or no to-date counts as open on that side. The existing `findAll(sheetId)` still marks no one as held, and that's what the add-member validation uses, since it doesn't work out cuts.
- **`pool/LoadPools.java`**: loads pools using the sheet's today, so the pool screen and each person's cut total both pick up holds.
- **`pool/PoolResponse.java`**: each member with a cut gets the pot × their share ÷ the shares of the members with a cut, added up, rounded half to even. The remainder still goes to the largest share among those members, earliest added on a tie. Held and retired members show 0.00, and if no one has a cut, everyone shows 0.00.

With no holds, the result is the same as before, because the divisor is still 100. The pool's total share and balance check didn't change, so a hold doesn't affect either one. Only people can be held; a pool that is a member of another pool still gets its cut as before.

There's no stored-data change: holds were already stored, and whether one is in force is worked out from today each time pools are loaded.
